comment: Datasets the quality benchmark downloads at run time. Nothing here is committed to the repository: each entry names the publisher's own URL, the SHA-256 and exact byte count of every download, and the reference products. A file whose bytes, hash and licence are not all recorded does not belong here. See DATASETS.md for why each was chosen and what was rejected.

aerial-nadir.title: Bandamaji, Grande Comore (Comoros) drone survey, 2023-06-26

licence.name: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International
licence.redistribution: allowed with attribution; this benchmark downloads only

reference_files.publisher_settings: OpenDroneMap: orthophoto-resolution=1 cm, dem-resolution=2.0 cm, dsm=true, auto-boundary=true

aerial-nadir.notes: The publisher states OpenDroneMap reconstructed 102 of 102 images at a 2.4 cm GSD over 0.048 km^2. Its ortho and DSM are both at 2.19 cm/px (the record quotes 1 and 2.0, which OpenDroneMap reads in centimetres), so the reference matches the imagery resolution rather than being coarser than it.
aerial-nadir.param_overrides_reason: Four measured limits, each with the run that found it. (1) 30 of 102 images: the full set at 20 MP spent over five hours in BuildDepthMaps. (2) MatchPhotos keypoint_limit_per_mpx=250: at the default 1000 the matching was killed out of memory at 97%. (3) BuildDepthMaps downscale=8: quarters the depth-map pixel count, leaving a 1.7 cm grid still finer than the 2.4 cm GSD the imagery justifies. (4) BuildOrthomosaic resolution=0.10 with refine_seamlines=false: the site is 0.048 km2, so 2.4 cm is 83 million cells and even 5 cm is 19 million, each cell carrying an alpha-expansion over 30 camera labels - both overran the stage budget. 10 cm is 4.8 million cells and a normal ortho deliverable, and the argmax seam labelling keeps the cost linear in cells; the trade is visible seams where the score steps, which the side-by-side comparison shows. The effective-resolution metric is reported against this nominal, so 'did the mosaic get softer' stays a valid signal. All four are recorded in every metrics JSON and printed in the report.
aerial-nadir.max_images_reason: The dense stage costs images x pixels, and 102 frames at 20 MP does not fit a weekly job on a shared CPU runner: the first run of this benchmark spent over five hours in BuildDepthMaps and was cancelled. 30 images is the contiguous block nearest the flight's centre by GPS, which is a real spatial strip with the overlap the stereo stage needs — a strided sample across the whole flight would only just overlap and would produce sparse depth maps for a reason that has nothing to do with the code. The 30 are chosen deterministically and named in the report.

terrestrial-laser.title: ETH3D high-res multi-view training scene 'terrains'
terrestrial-laser.publisher: ETH Zurich, Computer Vision and Geometry Group (Schops et al., CVPR 2017)
terrestrial-laser.flight: oblique handheld DSLR (ground-truth geometry reference, not a drone flight)

licence.name: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International
licence.redistribution: not allowed; the benchmark downloads inside the CI job only and never commits or publishes the data

terrestrial-laser.notes: The scan_eval archive holds the laser scan already aligned into the image frame, which is why it is used instead of the 1.9 GB full ground-truth bundle. The reconstruction is registered onto the scan by similarity ICP before scoring, because an SfM model has no metric scale and these images carry no GPS. ETH3D scores accuracy and completeness at 2/5/10 cm; this benchmark uses the same tolerances.
terrestrial-laser.param_overrides_reason: The same keypoint and depth-map budgets as the aerial set, for the same measured reason: at 24 MP per frame the default keypoint density killed the match stage out of memory. There is no ortho resolution override here — this dataset's reference is a laser cloud, and BuildOrthomosaic is only measured reference-free.
terrestrial-laser.max_images_reason: 42 frames at 24 MP is 64 million depth-map pixels at downscale 8 over 42 views, which does not fit the weekly budget on a shared CPU runner. 30 of the 42 is enough for a 30-view dense reconstruction of the scene while leaving headroom; the selection is deterministic and named in the report.
